newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: HERMIS WILL NOT REVISE 97 PROFIT FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: HERMIS WILL NOT REVISE 97 PROFIT FORECAST.

text.p: Lithuania's Hermis Bank said on Wednesday it was satisfied with its first half 1997 results and did not plan to revise its 1997 profit forecast.
"We are totally satisfied with the results for the first six months of the year and do not intend to revise our 1997 profit forecast," the chairwoman of the bank, Nadiezhda Novickiene told, Reuters.
The bank reported earlier on Wednesday that its net profit for the first six months of the year was 14.3 million litas.
Its net profit forecast for 1997 is 40.6 million litas. Its net profit for 1996 was 27.4 million litas.
"Our profit in the second half of the year will be higher and the growing assets of the bank will provide a good basis for profit growth," Novickiene said.
The bank's assets rose by 39 percent in the first six months of the year to 741.6 million litas.
She added that the bank's recent share capital increase will also provide it with more profit generating possibilities.
The bank recently raised its share capital by 23 million litas to 90 million litas. Part of the issue will be distributed as global depository receipts (GDRs).
The bank is the second largest private commericial bank in Lithuania.
